warnings: No formal upper limit is set for biotin; UK guidance considers 900 µg (0.9 mg) per day or less from supplements unlikely to cause harm.
High-dose biotin can cause false results in some blood tests, including troponin (heart attack test) and thyroid tests. Tell your doctor and the lab about any biotin product before a blood test.
Hair, skin and nail supplements often contain 5,000-10,000 µg of biotin, far more than the 40 µg daily target; benefit for hair or nails in healthy people is not proven.
Raw egg white contains avidin, which blocks biotin absorption; eat eggs cooked.
Long-term anti-seizure medicines can lower biotin; discuss with your doctor.
Biotin shampoos and hair oils do not count toward daily intake.
Hair fall needs a doctor's check for causes such as iron deficiency or thyroid problems before taking biotin.
General information, not medical advice. Check with a doctor before starting supplements.
